title: Pick One Before Midnight
amb: crackling bonfire, tiki torches hissing, distant waves, party chatter under deep house; later night wind on a rooftop, string lights buzzing faintly, crickets

lines.text: Seven gorgeous men. Three of them are millionaires looking for a wife.
The bonfire cracks. Sparks drift past your face. The clock above the bar says eleven fifty-five.
The other four are broke... and faking it for a million dollars.
Fall for a fake, and he's the one you fly home with.
She lifts a blank cream card and turns it slowly, so everyone can see there's nothing on it.
At midnight, ladies, you couple up. Same suite. Same team. And when you vote, everyone hears it.
Heels click on stone right behind you. Perfume, sweet and sharp.
Champagne dress, night one? Bold. Shame you won't make it to Friday.
"Then I'd better work fast," you tell her.
Fast. Cute. I'll try to remember you.
Ice rattles in a shaker. A glass lands beside your hand, cold against your knuckles.
Ignore her. I'm Wes. This one's yours. Lime, no sugar, no tiny umbrella.
Earlier you told a stranger at check-in that you hate sweet drinks. You never told him.
I listen. Also, the girl at check-in talks a lot. Mostly the first one, though.
You ask him straight out whether he's real or fake.
Ask me again in a week. I'll still be here.
[chuckles softly] That came out fast, didn't it? I practiced it in the mirror. Kidding. Mostly.
Before he made the drink, he flicked the shaker, caught it, and poured, all in one easy motion. You remember that.
Up on the stairs, someone isn't drinking or smiling. He's just watching you.
You want a straight answer? Not down there.
You set the glass down on the bar and leave it there. The wooden steps creak under your bare feet.
On the roof the wind is cooler. String lights hum, the ocean is a long way off, and the crickets are loud. He leans on the rail and doesn't turn around.
Everyone down there's selling something. Even the ones who don't need to.
You ask him what he's selling.
Nothing. Would you believe me either way?
[quietly] Ask me a better question. Why'd you come here?
You tell him you came for a real one, not a check.
For a second, the corner of his mouth moves.
Huh. That's not what they usually say.
Down below, a gong. The music cuts out. In the quiet, all you can hear is the torches hissing.
Midnight, everyone. Ladies, step up. And our front-runner goes first.
Back by the fire, every face turns toward you. Wes stands by the bar, his grin a little too ready. Jasper stays at the edge of the light with his arms folded.
[softly] Choose carefully. Whoever you don't take... is mine.
She means it. Her fingers are already drifting toward both of them.
No pressure. I'm just the guy who already knows how you take your coffee. Black, right?
Pick for a reason. Not a face.
One choice. Two men. And the whole island watching. So. Who's it going to be?

prompt: 午夜钟声刚落，Mei 等你开口，Sloane 等着把剩下那个挽走。你走向谁？
choices: 我穿过篝火，牵起 Wes 的手：就你了
我走到火光边的 Jasper 面前：我选你
